Exercise A

Polite or too blunt?

Choose the best option for each gap. Think about the reader: is the wording neutral, polite and clear?

Part 1: Parts of emails

1. Dear Ms Clark, I am writing 1 the internship you advertised last week.

2. Could you 2 me some information about the course?

3. I was wondering 3 it is possible to visit the flat on Saturday.

4. Would you mind 4 me the form?

5. Thank you for your 5.

Part 2: Choose the best sentence

6. To a gym manager: 6

7. To the exam office: 7

8. To the library: 8

9. The first line of an email to a landlord: 9

10. After a quick answer: Thank you 10 your quick reply.

Exercise B

Reply to an email

Read the email below and write a short, polite reply in 60–80 words.

The email you received

Subject: Your room request

Dear student,

The seminar room you asked about is booked on Thursday. It is free on Friday at 10:00 or on Monday at 14:00. Please tell me which time you prefer.

Kind regards,
Dr Hall

Word count: 0 (aim for 60–80)

Choose a time, thank Dr Hall and ask one polite question, for example about the key.
